#### Mar 3, 2026

## Plain's MCP

Image

Update, November 2026: Plain’s MCP server now has 400+ tools. See the MCP server docs for the current list.

You can now connect AI tools like Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor directly to your Plain workspace using the Plain MCP server. Once connected, your AI assistant can read threads, look up customers, check tenant details, and browse your help center. It can also take actions: reply to threads, assign them, change priority, add labels, create notes, and mark threads as done.

At launch, the server included 30 tools across threads, customers, tenants, help center articles, and workspace data. You authenticate with your existing Plain account, so the MCP server has the same permissions as your user.

To get started, check out the setup guide.

pages.title: AI Agents - Does the Plain MCP server support API key authentication? | Help Center (https://help.plain.com/article/does-the-plain-mcp-server-support-api-key-authentication-h7d83qtfdzxo4h49x4oyklwx)
pages.text: AI Agents - Does the Plain MCP server support API key authentication? | Help Center How can I help you? This conversation will be visible to Plain employees Does the Plain MCP server support API key authentication? Updated 2 Sep 2026 by Plain Copy No. The Plain Model Context Protocol (MCP) server at https://mcp.plain.com/mcp supports OAuth only. How authentication works You authenticate with your existing Plain account through OAuth. The MCP session inherits your permissions, and replies and actions appear under your user, as in the app. This ties MCP activity to a real user for audit and attribution. Each person who uses the server needs a Plain account with any role, including Viewer, and must complete the OAuth flow once in their MCP client, such as Cursor, Claude or ChatGPT. There is no shared credential that lets several engineers connect. Use a custom MCP server with a machine user API key To give a team of engineers access to Plain data without individual Viewer accounts, build a lightweight custom MCP server that wraps Plain's GraphQL API with a single machine user API key. In Settings, open Machine Users and create a machine user with read-only permissions. Generate an API key for that machine user. Build an MCP server that uses the key to call Plain's GraphQL API and exposes the tools your team needs. Point your engineers' MCP clients at your custom server. The trade-off is that all activity goes through the machine user, so there is no per-engineer attribution in your workspace timeline. Related documentation MCP server Machine users

pages.title: Developer & API - Migrating to accounts with the Plain API | Help Center (https://help.plain.com/article/migrating-to-accounts-api)
pages.text: Developer & API - Migrating to accounts with the Plain API | Help Center How can I help you? This conversation will be visible to Plain employees Migrating to accounts with the Plain API Updated 4 Nov 2026 by Juan Copy Accounts replace companies in the Plain API, and they are the new name for tenants. This article lists the GraphQL fields, operations, permissions, webhooks, and customer card request to update in your integration. For the steps inside your workspace, see Migrating companies and tenants to accounts . The product UI switches its labels from tenants to accounts between October 26 and November 1, 2026. What an account is An account is the organization a customer belongs to. A customer can belong to more than one account. Read those memberships from accountMemberships on the customer. See Accounts in the docs. Each account record includes: name externalId primaryDomain and alternateDomains accountFields logoUrl In GraphQL, source is API , SALESFORCE , HUBSPOT , ATTIO , or EMAIL_DOMAIN . Webhook payloads use api , salesforce , hubspot , attio , or email_domain . Store a company account owner in a user reference account field. The field type is USER_REFERENCE_TYPE . Tiers and their SLAs apply to an account. Set the tier with updateAccountTier . HubSpot, Salesforce, and Attio map a CRM company to an account and a company attribute to an account field. See CRM . Fields Account inputs add accountIdentifier , accountIdentifiers , accountId , accountIds , and accountFields . Plain marks the tenant and company fields they replace as deprecated, and those fields still work. Send one name per field in a request, not both. Use Instead of accountIdentifier tenantIdentifier , companyIdentifier accountIdentifiers tenantIdentifiers , companyIdentifiers accountId tenantId , companyId accountIds tenantIds , companyIds accountFields tenantFields account tenant , company accounts tenants , companies on a saved view hasAccounts hasCompany , hasTenants hasAccountFieldExternalIds hasTenantFieldExternalIds accountMemberships tenantMemberships , and company on a customer accountMembershipPolicy tenantMembershipPolicy customerAccounts customerCompany , customerTenants These inputs accept the new fields: CreateThreadInput and CreateThreadFromSlackMessageInput accept accountIdentifier . UpsertCustomerOnCreateInput accepts accountIdentifiers . ThreadsFilter , CustomersFilter , and ThreadMetricFilters accept accountIdentifiers . ThreadsFilter and ThreadMetricFilters also accept accountFields . CreateTaskInput , UpdateTaskInput , and TierMemberIdentifierInput accept accountId . TasksFilter , ThreadClustersFilter , ThreadLinkGroupFilter , and BroadcastAudienceFilterInput accept accountIds . SavedThreadsViewFilterInput accepts accounts and accountFields . ThreadsDisplayOptionsInput accepts hasAccounts and hasAccountFieldExternalIds . Thread exposes account . ThreadChannelAssociation exposes accountId and accountMembershipPolicy . Help center access settings accept accountIds . Portal thread visibility accepts customerAccounts and overrideCustomerAccounts . Grouping and access enums use ACCOUNT where they used COMPANY or TENANT : ThreadsGroupBy and ThreadMetricGroupBy use ACCOUNT . ThreadMetricGroupBy.ACCOUNT_FIELD replaces TENANT_FIELD and needs subKey set to the field's external ID. DiscussionSourceEntityType and ThreadScopePrimitiveType use ACCOUNT . ThreadScopePrimitiveType is the dimension on a custom role access filter. Operations Call the account operation. Plain marks the tenant and company operations as deprecated, and each deprecation reason names the account operation. Account operation Replaces accounts tenants , companies account tenant , company searchAccounts searchTenants , searchCompanies accountFieldSchemas tenantFieldSchemas createAccount createTenant upsertAccount upsertTenant , upsertCompany deleteAccount deleteTenant , deleteCompany addCustomerToAccounts addCustomerToTenants removeCustomerFromAccounts removeCustomerFromTenants setCustomerAccounts setCustomerTenants , updateCustomerCompany updateAccountTier updateTenantTier , updateCompanyTier importAccounts importTenants updateThreadAccount updateThreadTenant upsertAccountField upsertTenantField upsertAccountFieldSchema upsertTenantFieldSchema deleteAccountField deleteTenantField deleteAccountFieldSchema deleteTenantFieldSchema importAccountFieldSchemas importTenantFieldSchemas importAccountFieldSchemasFromService importTenantFieldSchemasFromService setupAccountFieldSchemaMapping setupTenantFieldSchemaMapping removeAccountFieldSchemaMapping removeTenantFieldSchemaMapping updateThreadChannelAssociationAccountMembershipPolicy updateThreadChannelAssociationTenantMembershipPolicy The @team-plain/graphql SDK exposes upsertAccount on client.mutation . upsertTenant and upsertCompany are deprecated and point at upsertAccount . The current calls are documented under Accounts in the API docs. Permissions Account calls use tenant permission strings. accounts , account , and searchAccounts need tenant:read . createAccount needs tenant:create . upsertAccount needs tenant:create and tenant:edit . deleteAccount needs tenant:delete . Account field calls use tenantField and tenantFieldSchema strings. deleteAccountField needs tenant:edit . Adding or removing a customer needs customer:edit plus customerTenantMembership:create or customerTenantMembership:delete . Account fields lists the field strings for each call. The companies , company , and searchCompanies queries need company:read . upsertCompany needs company:create and company:edit . deleteCompany needs company:delete . The API docs page for each account call lists the strings it needs. Webhooks Account events ship in webhook version 2026-10-06 and later. A target on an earlier version, including an unversioned target, does not receive them. Move the target to 2026-10-06 or later. The events are: account.account_created account.account_updated account.account_deleted account.account_membership_changed account.account_field_created account.account_field_updated account.account_field_deleted thread.thread_tenant_updated keeps its event type. The payload includes tenant and previousTenant . Customer cards The unversioned customer card request has no version field. It sends the account under tenant , with id and externalId . Request format 2026-10-19 sets version to "2026-10-19" and sends that same object under account . The full request is in request versions . Update your customer card API so it reads account when version is 2026-10-19 . Go to Settings > Customer cards and set Request format to 2026-10-19 . The setting applies to every customer card in the workspace. You can switch back to unversioned if your API needs more time. Changing the format reloads every card the next time it is viewed. Plain doesn't reuse cards cached under the other format. Configuration Saved views, workflows, custom role access filters, and help center access lists that reference a company show an "Accounts are replacing companies" hint. Plain converts them to the matching account settings. Replace an Assign to company account owner workflow step with Assign to user , and select a user reference account field. Compatibility Deprecated tenant and company fields and operations still work. The deprecation reason on each one names the account field or operation to call. Move your integration to those names.

pages.title: AI Agents - Can the Sidekick Agent use tools from a custom MCP server? | Help Center (https://help.plain.com/article/how-sidekick-accesses-tools-through-a-custom-mcp-server-8hjeeea72nrok0hn0lp7qkx9)
pages.text: AI Agents - Can the Sidekick Agent use tools from a custom MCP server? | Help Center How can I help you? This conversation will be visible to Plain employees Can the Sidekick Agent use tools from a custom MCP server? Updated 27 Oct 2026 by Plain Copy Yes. When you register a custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, the Sidekick Agent calls tools/list on the server URL and treats the tools it finds like any native connector, such as Linear or Datadog. Calls go through a trusted proxy and are brokered server-side, so your credentials never enter the agent's sandbox. Authentication OAuth : Plain brokers the OAuth flow. Users authorize once and the agent reuses the token. API key : You provide the key name, value and placement, header or query parameter. The key is vaulted and injected at call time. Things to know Workspace-wide scope : Connections are shared by all users in the workspace. There is no per-user authentication. Everyone calls the server with the same credentials. HTTPS required : Your server must be reachable over HTTPS at a public URL. Servers on a private network need a public tunnel such as ngrok or Cloudflare Tunnel. Tool list is cached : the Sidekick Agent snapshots the tool list when you connect. If your server's tools change, reconnect it in Sidekick Agent, under Integrations. Limit : Up to 10 custom MCP servers per workspace. Internal MCP gateway You can route the Sidekick Agent through an internal MCP gateway for tools such as Slack, Git or Grafana instead of connecting to each directly. The gateway controls authentication, access scoping and rate limiting, and the agent gets exactly the access it grants. Related documentation Tools & integrations MCP server

pages.title: Plain — Plain's MCP Server: Connect Any AI Tool to Your Support Data (https://changelog.plain.com/blog/mcp-server)
pages.text: Plain â Plain's MCP Server: Connect Any AI Tool to Your Support Data Product Solutions Resources Customers Pricing Sign in Book a demo Blog / Product Plain's MCP Server: Connect Any AI Tool to Your Support Data Susana de Sousa Community, Plain Published On Mar 4, 2026 Update, November 2026: Plainâs MCP server now has 400+ tools. See the MCP server docs for the current list. A customer writes in. You open the thread, read through the back-and-forth, check their profile, pull up their company's other threads to see if there's a pattern, then dig through your help center to find the article you half-remember updating last quarter. By the time you've assembled enough context to respond, ten minutes have passed and you haven't actually helped anyone yet. That's the problem MCP solves. What we shipped Plain now has an MCP server. If you use Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or any other AI tool that supports the MCP standard, it can talk directly to your Plain workspace. Your threads, your customers, your help center, all accessible from the AI tools you already have open. Here's the same scenario with Plain's MCP server connected: You open Claude, type "What's going on with this customer?", and it pulls their recent threads, looks up their profile, checks the tenant's other threads, finds the relevant help center article, and drafts a response with the right details. One prompt instead of ten minutes of digging. (If MCP is a new term for you, we wrote a plain-language guide to what it is and how it works for support teams.) What your AI can actually do With Plain's MCP server connected, your AI tools can do the same things you do in Plain's UI, on your behalf. At launch, we built 30 tools across five areas: Threads. Fetch, search, reply, assign, snooze, change priority, add labels, mark done, create internal notes. The daily workflow stuff that eats your time when you're doing it manually across dozens of threads. Customers. Look up profiles, search by name or email, pull a customer's full thread history. Tenants. Search and manage company-level data. Spot patterns across all of a company's threads. Useful when you're trying to figure out whether an issue is a one-off or part of something bigger. Help center. Browse articles, find stale content, create or update articles directly. You can flag articles that haven't been updated in 90 days and draft new ones from recurring questions. Workspace. Access your user profile, workspace settings, and available labels. BYOA and MCP: two sides of the same idea Last month we launched Bring Your Own Agent: connect any AI agent to Plain's infrastructure. This month, MCP. BYOA is about what happens inside Plain. Your AI agent triages threads, replies to customers, manages queues. It works autonomously within your support workflow. MCP is about what happens outside Plain. The AI tools your team already uses (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor) can now reach into Plain alongside your other work tools. Support data lives in the same conversation as your code, your bugs, and your team chat. Where the real value shows up Plain on its own gets you thread lookups and customer context. Add GitHub, Linear, Slack, and other platforms through MCP and the AI can trace a customer issue from ticket to pull request to deploy to team channel without you opening any of them. A support agent asks about a customer issue. The AI checks thread history in Plain, finds the related pull request in GitHub, confirms the fix shipped in Linear, and posts an update to Slack. No tab-switching. No reassembling context from four different tools. That removes the manual glue work that makes support feel like an information logistics job instead of a customer job. A good starting prompt: "show me what's assigned to me and summarize the top five by urgency." It works immediately because it's read-only and obvious. From there, try pulling in customer context alongside threads so the AI can draft replies with the right details, and start approving write actions. You stay in control The server includes both read and write tools. Most AI clients will ask for your confirmation before executing write actions like replying or assigning. You can start with read-only prompts and work your way up to writes as you build trust in the workflow. Authentication uses your existing Plain account. No separate API keys to generate or rotate. The AI inherits your permissions, so it can only access what you can access in Plain. Get started The MCP server is live at mcp.plain.com/mcp . Setup instructions for Claude.ai, Claude Code, Cursor, and ChatGPT are in our help center guide . If you're new to MCP entirely, start with our plain-language explainer . We built Plain's MCP server because we believe support tools should work with any AI, not lock you into one vendor's ecosystem. pages.title: Plain — MCP for Customer Support: Platforms and Permissions (2026) (https://changelog.plain.com/blog/mcp-customer-support-2026)
pages.text: Plain â MCP for Customer Support: Platforms and Permissions (2026) Product Solutions Resources Customers Pricing Sign in Book a demo Blog / Support Engineering MCP for Customer Support: Platforms and Permissions (2026) Cole D'Ambra Head of Growth & Demand Generation Last Updated Nov 18, 2026 Published On Mar 6, 2026 MCP for customer support means your support platform runs an MCP server, so the AI client your team already uses (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor) can read customer context and act on threads through one standard interface, without an integration layer you build and maintain. Which platforms have a server matters less than whose access each connection runs under, because that decides what the AI can see, what it can change and whose name goes on a reply. Plain is the agentic infrastructure for customer work, a B2B customer support and help desk platform, and its MCP server signs each person in with their own Plain account over OAuth, so a connection carries that person's permissions and no one else's. As of November 2026, Plain's MCP server has 400+ tools . What is MCP for customer support? MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard for connecting AI applications to outside systems. A platform runs an MCP server that describes its tools: a name, a description and an input schema for each. An AI client connects, authenticates and calls those tools when a request needs them, so nobody has to write code against the platform's API first. If the protocol itself is new to you, start with our plain-language MCP explainer . Direction matters when you compare vendors. A server lets AI clients you choose work with the support platform's data. A client lets the platform's own AI call other systems' servers. Zendesk's August 10, 2026 release is a client: admins connect Zendesk to public or private MCP servers and pick which tools its AI features can use in action flows. That release lets Zendesk's AI reach other systems; on its own, it isn't a way for your AI client to reach Zendesk. MCP sits on top of the API a platform already has. For Plain that's the GraphQL API , which is why API-first infrastructure matters for AI agents : an MCP server can only expose what the API underneath can do. On our evaluation calls, buyers who ask about MCP usually ask about API access in the same breath: they treat MCP as one door into the platform, not the whole point. Whose access does an MCP connection inherit? It depends on how the server authenticates, and vendors answer this in a few different ways. On our recent evaluation calls, a question that kept coming up was about access itself: who a connection signs in as, what it can reach, or who has to approve it. It's the right question to ask first, before tool counts. Platform How a connection signs in Whose permissions it carries Source (checked October 28, 2026) Plain MCP server OAuth only, each person once per client The signed-in person's Plain role; replies and actions appear under that user Plain help article Intercom MCP server OAuth (recommended) or a Bearer token Fin Operator tools are "authorized as you" and need OAuth; not stated for the other tools Intercom developer guide Intercom Fin Agent API MCP server A workspace Fin Agent API key The calling service supplies the end user's identity in the request Intercom help article Front MCP server OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, via a directory connector or an OAuth app a Front admin creates The authorizing teammate's role, within the read, write and send permissions the admin allows Front developer docs , Front help center Freshworks MCP server for Freshdesk API key only Not stated in source Freshdesk MCP article Dynamics 365 Customer Experience MCP Server for Service Through Microsoft's Agent 365 Tooling Gateway Existing Dataverse roles and permissions Microsoft Learn These models behave differently when something goes wrong. With per-person OAuth, a connection can't do more than the person who made it, and every action traces to a named user. With a key, the key's own permissions apply to whoever holds it, so who holds it becomes the real access decision. With a gateway, access follows the platform's existing role model, and the gateway is one more component to configure. Front adds a fourth pattern: an admin sets the outer limit on read, write and send, and each teammate stays inside their own role. What Plain's model means in practice Plain's MCP server docs say the server "has the same permissions as your user," and that replies to threads "will appear as though they come from your user." The help article adds the part buyers ask about most: An admin's connection is the admin's alone. Each person who uses the server completes the OAuth flow once in their own client. There is no shared credential that lets several people connect, so an admin connecting Claude doesn't hand admin access to anyone else. Any role can connect, including Viewer.
